items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Tom and his sister went to the pond. They looked for frogs. Tom found one sitting on a log. His sister found two by the reeds.

Who found more frogs — Tom or his sister?
items.answer: Tom's sister found more frogs. She found two, while Tom found one.

steps: Read the story and find the number of frogs each person found.
Tom found one frog. His sister found two frogs.
Two is more than one, so his sister found more.

Why does Clover thump his back foot?
items.answer: Clover thumps his back foot when he is happy.

steps: Look for the sentence that tells you why Clover thumps.
The text says: 'Clover would thump his back foot when he was happy.'
The answer is directly stated in the story.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

'Snowflakes'
Down they fall, one by one,
White and cold, blocking the sun.
They pile up on the ground so deep,
The whole wide world goes off to sleep.

What do the snowflakes do in this poem?
items.answer: The snowflakes fall one by one, cover the ground, and make the world seem quiet and sleepy.

steps: Read the poem and look for what the snowflakes do.
They fall, they are white and cold, they pile up on the ground.
The poem also says the world 'goes off to sleep,' which shows things get quiet.

Where were the three bears when Goldilocks came inside?
items.answer: The three bears were out on a walk when Goldilocks came inside.

steps: Read the first two sentences carefully.
The text says: 'Papa Bear, Mama Bear, and Baby Bear went for a walk.'
That is where they were — on a walk.

items.prompt:

Sasha got a new library card. She walked to the library by herself for the first time. She chose three books about space. She carried them home in her backpack and read all weekend.

What did Sasha do with her new library card?
items.answer: Sasha used her library card to go to the library by herself and check out three books about space.

steps: Read the story to find what Sasha does.
She walked to the library, chose books about space, and took them home.

items.prompt:
Read the fable below.

A mouse ran over a sleeping lion. The lion woke up and caught the mouse. 'Please let me go,' the mouse squeaked. 'One day I will help you.' The lion laughed but let him go. Later, the lion was caught in a net. The mouse heard his roar, ran over, and chewed through the ropes. The lion was free.

How did the mouse help the lion?
items.answer: The mouse chewed through the ropes of the net that had trapped the lion and set him free.

steps: Look for the part of the story where the mouse helps.
The lion was caught in a net and roared for help.
The mouse came and chewed through the ropes to free him.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

'Spring'
The birds are back,
The flowers grew,
The mud is thick,
The sky is blue.
I smell the rain
That was not snow,
And everything begins to grow.

What season is this poem about?
items.answer: The poem is about spring. Clues include birds coming back, flowers growing, mud, blue sky, rain instead of snow, and things beginning to grow.

steps: Look for clues about the season in the poem.
Birds coming back, flowers, mud, rain instead of snow, and things growing are all signs of spring.
The poem names all the things that happen at the start of spring.

What did Mike make for breakfast?
items.answer: Mike made toast with butter and orange juice for breakfast.

steps: Read the story and list what Mike made.

These are the breakfast items he prepared.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

The three little pigs each built a house. One used straw. One used sticks. One used bricks. When the wolf came, he blew down the straw house and the stick house. But he could not blow down the brick house.

Which house was the strongest?
items.answer: The brick house was the strongest. The wolf blew down the straw and stick houses, but he could not blow down the brick house.

steps: Look for which house survived the wolf's blowing.
Straw: blown down. Sticks: blown down. Bricks: NOT blown down.
The brick house was the strongest because the wolf could not destroy it.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Grace wanted to feed the ducks at the pond. She tore up old bread and put it in a bag. When she got to the pond, five ducks swam over right away. She tossed the bread and they gobbled it up. Two more ducks swam over too late — the bread was all gone.

How many ducks came to eat the bread?
items.answer: Five ducks came right away and ate the bread. Two more arrived too late and did not get any. Seven ducks came in total.

steps: Count the ducks: five came right away, two came late.
Five plus two equals seven ducks in total.
The bread was gone before the last two arrived.

And fly to that place.

items.answer: According to the poem, books can take you anywhere in the world — jungles, deserts, oceans, and space — without leaving the library.

The poem says you can 'go anywhere' and 'fly to that place' by opening a book.

Jordan got on the bus after school. He chose a seat by the window. A new kid got on and stood in the aisle, looking unsure. Jordan moved his backpack. 'You can sit here,' he said. The new kid smiled and sat down.

Why did Jordan move his backpack?
items.answer: Jordan moved his backpack to make room for the new kid to sit beside him.

steps: Look at what happens just before Jordan moves his backpack.
A new kid is standing in the aisle looking unsure.
Jordan moves his bag and invites the new kid to sit — he is being kind.

Penny was nervous about the first day at her new school. She did not know anyone. At lunch, a girl named Dani sat next to her. 'My name is Dani. What's yours?' she asked. Penny smiled for the first time all day.

Why did Penny smile at lunch?
items.answer: Penny smiled because Dani sat next to her and introduced herself. Penny had been nervous and did not know anyone, and Dani's kindness made her feel better.

steps: Look for what happens right before Penny smiles.
Dani sits next to her and asks her name.
Penny smiles 'for the first time all day' — Dani's friendly act made her feel welcome.
